with_skill hits 100% pass rate on all 3 evals; without_skill failures concentrate almost entirely in the mechanics the skill exists to enforce (strict Gherkin syntax, GitHub sub-issue structure, story-map/story labels) rather than in map/story reasoning quality — the baseline wrote comparably good backbones and even flagged idea ambiguity on its own in eval 2.

Eval 2 (vague-recipe-idea) is non-discriminating as currently scored: both configs hit 3/3 because its 3 assertions only check whether the ambiguity was flagged, which a generic competent agent handled just as well. The real gap observed between runs — with_skill went all the way through slicing, Gherkin, and publish; without_skill stopped at the map — isn’t captured by any assertion on this eval. Recommend adding a slice/Gherkin assertion to eval 2 before the next iteration.

Cross-run contamination: all 6 subagents ran concurrently against one shared test repo (dominicfarr/story-map-skill-test). Eval 3’s without_skill baseline explicitly said it inferred the story-map label and issue title convention from other issues already created by concurrent with_skill runs in that same repo, which partially inflates its apparent similarity to the skill’s GitHub structure on that one dimension. The deeper checks (Gherkin, sub-issues) still correctly failed for it, so this didn’t flip any verdict, but future iterations should give each run its own repo or clone to keep the comparison clean.

with_skill runs take roughly 2.3x without_skill’s average wall time (116s vs 51s) and about 17% more tokens — expected, since the skill always pushes through to GitHub-structured BDD specs. The without_skill average is pulled down by eval 2’s baseline (31s), which only got there by stopping short of BDD and publish, so it isn’t an apples-to-apples speed comparison.

without_skill pass rate has high variance (0.29 to 1.0, stddev 0.37) across evals, swinging entirely on how much GitHub/BDD structure a given task happened to pull out of it rather than on reasoning quality, which was consistently solid across all three without_skill runs.
